reviewable_adoption_proposal.policy: Use the same D profile on every role; mathematical omission rules only

primary_reference: stable BASE (B), controlled with the unchanged R146 PE
decision_discussion: Recommend standalone GD (D) as one uniform paper-enhancement candidate for author review. Against controlled stable BASE, it improves the physical incumbent on both entered difficult roles (RB35 by 2.5415%, K35 by 3.1283%) and reduces both relative gaps. It avoids the measured STOCK+GD combination's RB35 incumbent regression. The important remaining tradeoff is K35 supported L: D lowers it by .011455146913 (2.0300%), even while U and gap improve. K20 keeps the same U and remains open with slightly weaker L; RX20 retains certification with a 2.341246s delay. These measured disadvantages are retained rather than hidden in an aggregate score. The two hard-role incumbent/gap gains, with no observed incumbent regression on any of the four roles, support this bounded uniform recommendation; this is not a general proof-speed or dominance claim. D does not retain STOCK's strong K20 certificate benefit. S/SD remain valuable sealed research references, and no role-specific D/SD switching is proposed. The concrete proposal is the new standalone entry/profile for the next enhanced paper version; stable R137 and its manuscript retain their original bytes pending author review of the Draft PR.
core_discussion: K20 B and D both return U=.7168065462777502 and remain open after their complete cap1200 windows. Supported L changes from .7047916969720031 to .7042027654726336; the relative gap increases from 1.676163% to 1.758324% (+.082160 percentage points). This is not a useful standalone certificate gain. The sealed same-PE S/SD cells certify the same U in 94.261389/74.916420s; their strong proof advantage is preserved as a real counterpoint. RB35 D instead returns U/L=.3358835889496765/.21947515015073324 against sealed same-PE B=.34464262559194814/.2189859496034747. U improves 2.5414838421%, L rises .0004892005473, and gap falls from 36.459993% to 34.657376% (-1.8026165231 percentage points). The L gain is small; the main independent benefit is physical incumbent quality. All four RB35 cells are open. D improves U and gap against SD but has lower L than SD's .23349894443616206, so it does not dominate the combination at both ends. Actual new D models have two GD rows and zero STOCK rows; the comparison is not inferred from method labels.
trajectory_discussion: The committed physical-witness records locate the hard-role benefit in finding better incumbents, not certification. RB35 D already has U=.3372904684849699 at 668.391s, below B's eventual final U, and reaches its own final U at 1346.250s. B reaches its different final U at 2366.781s. K35 D first beats B's final U at 1338.656s with U=.6791034678575588; B reaches its final U at 1758.516s. D then has U=.6767988451958106 at 1686.187s and finds the final .671179796420249 at 2364.047s. That last improvement is near cap and is disclosed; the earlier strict gains establish that the benefit does not arise solely from the last seconds. Different-quality final-U discovery times are not convergence speedup ratios. K20 reaches the common final U at 224.546s for B and 417.765s for D. D's 16.338s lower complete total there is mainly a verification-cost decrease (49.467897 to 33.581330s), not faster proof. All 14 entered/reused formal cells have zero outer splits. Native root-after-cuts values, simplex, Work and node differences describe changed search but do not identify a unique cause. For example, K35's printed root bound rises .42856 to .44681 and root simplex increases 5188 to 11374, while final supported L is lower; stronger root information does not force stronger final proof.
historical_discussion: R146's positive S→SD findings remain unchanged: K20 certifies about 20.52% sooner at the same U; RX20 retains certification with a small absolute 2.702614s certificate gain; RB35 improves U by 5.8283%, increases L by .004317345 and lowers gap by 4.6781 percentage points. Against BASE, that same SD pressure result had U higher by 9.6257%, L higher by .014512995 and gap larger by 1.7379 percentage points, a mixed tradeoff rather than two-end regression. RX20 SD's approximately 3.02e-9 positive U−L remains certified under the original R134 policy; no new floating-point repair or solve is introduced. R138's K15/K20 STOCK certificate benefits, its disclosed V2 transport identity in the finite Seed1 evidence, R144's RN-P K35 gains and R145's structural complementarity/root-retention results remain at their original versions. The Seed1 history is not a pure seed-only intervention, and no universal STOCK regression law is inferred. The strong historical RN-P K35 incumbent remains a research reference; no new matched RN-P bridge or claim of D beating every research variant is made. Fixed-domain K20 LP interaction remains a numerical fact, not complete-search synergy or general supermodularity.
extension_discussion: After both core roles completed, the real RB35 independent incumbent gain justified the finite extension with the same D profile. RX20 B/D both certify U=.6453250303858205. Certificate times are 22.324898/24.666144s: D is slower by 2.341246s (10.4872%); complete totals are 23.674241/26.345340s (+2.671099s). This small absolute delay preserves the certified role and is not used as a one-cell veto. The frozen K35 B/D cap2400 pair then returns U=.6928543586313136/.671179796420249, supported L=.5642907958373754/.5528356489241707 and gap=18.555640%/17.632257%. U improves 3.1282999004% and gap falls .9233832014 percentage points, while L decreases .0114551469132 (2.0300077545%). Both remain open; total costs 2374.928960/2378.192407s differ by 3.263447s and are not convergence times. This is an explicit incumbent/bound tradeoff, not two-end dominance. Stop the finite selection study here. Seven new full own-H arms and the seven sealed references are sufficient for this scoped candidate recommendation; no automatic 24-configuration/120-position panel, full K35 factorial, extra seed, K15 boundary, current S/SD clock repeat or RN-P bridge is needed. There is no material decision resting on a tiny cross-round clock difference. Unused budget is not unfinished work. Wider claims would require separately justified validation; that is not asserted or queued by this completed study.
navigation_discussion: Seven new own-H positions establish real standalone hard-role incumbent gains: RB35 U improves 2.54% and K35 U improves 3.13%, with smaller relative gaps on both. K35 supported L is 2.03% lower, K20 does not gain certification, and RX20 retains certification with a small 2.34s delay. Recommend one uniform standalone-GD paper enhancement candidate for author review, while preserving stable R137 and the strong historical STOCK/combination references. The claim is limited to four known Seed0 roles, with no instance-specific switching.
